units.subject: Biology
units.title: Exam Revision: Adaptation and Adaptive Colouration
objectives: Recall adaptation concepts previously taught in SS2 Biology and relate features to survival in a habitat.
Construct concise WAEC, NECO and JAMB responses explaining structural, physiological and behavioural adaptations and colouration.
units.body:
EXAM-PREPARATION REVISION BRIEF — PRIOR-LEARNING REVIEW ONLY

This unit revises adaptation concepts already present in the supplied SS2 First-Term Biology curriculum. It is not a new SS3 instructional topic. Adaptation refers to inherited structural, physiological or behavioural features that improve an organism's ability to survive and reproduce in a particular environment. An answer should connect each feature to the environmental challenge it helps an organism meet.

Structural adaptations are physical features, such as body shape, protective coverings, modified limbs or leaf structures. Physiological adaptations concern internal processes, while behavioural adaptations are actions that improve survival. Examples should be drawn only from the previously taught SS2 habitat and adaptation material. Protective or cryptic colouration helps an organism blend with its surroundings and may reduce detection by predators; warning colouration can make an organism conspicuous to potential predators, while mimicry may resemble another organism or object. Behavioural responses such as hiding, burrowing, migration or activity at particular times can reduce exposure to danger or unfavourable conditions.

EXAM RESPONSE METHOD
For a question asking for examples, name the organism, identify the feature or behaviour, and state the survival advantage. For a comparison, use the same basis on both sides. Avoid listing an adaptation without explaining its function. Use labelled diagrams only where the question requests them and ensure each label points to the correct structure.

SOURCE BOUNDARY
The SS3 Second-Term source scheme includes adaptation for survival and adaptive colouration/behaviour in Weeks 3–4. These are included here strictly as recall of prior SS2 adaptation content. Fruit classification, variation, evolution, genetics, chromosomes and probability are not included because their instructional coverage in the available SS2 source record has not been established. No new instruction on those topics is introduced.

practice.question_locator: SS3 Second-Term Biology source, Week Three evaluation: structural adaptations for obtaining food in animals.
practice.question: Give three examples of structural adaptation for obtaining food in animals.
practice.answer_locator: Authored model answer; examples require cross-check against the exact SS2 source lesson before release.
practice.answer: Examples may include a bird's beak adapted to its food, sharp claws or talons used to seize prey, and specialised teeth used to cut, tear or grind food. Explain how each feature assists feeding.
practice.explanation: Award credit for three valid structural features and their feeding functions; verify named examples against prior SS2 material before student release.

marking.criterion: One valid structural adaptation and correct feeding function.
